'''Shahina Agha Ghazanfar''' (born 1949) is a [[Pakistanis|Pakistani]] [[Botany|botanist]] and author best known for her work on plants from the [[Arabian Peninsula]], [[Pakistan]] and [[East Africa]].<ref name=":0" />

== Education ==
Ghazanfar studied at the [[University of the Punjab]] and the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Ghazanfar, Shahina Agha (1949–) |url=https://plants.jstor.org/stable/10.5555/al.ap.person.bm000066752 |access-date=13 June 2023 |website=JSTOR Plants |doi=}}</ref>

== Professional life ==
Ghazanfar lectured in botany at [[Kinnaird College for Women|Kinnaird College]] in Lahore and at [[State University of New York]]. She then worked as a curator and researcher at the [[National Herbarium, Pakistan|National Herbarium]] in Islamabad.<ref name=":0" />

From 1983, Ghazanfar lectured at [[Bayero University Kano|Bayero University]] in Nigeria, where she was keeper of the botanical garden. She founded the herbarium of the university, specialising in collecting plants from northern Nigeria.<ref name=":0" />

In 1987, she became associate professor at [[Sultan Qaboos University]] in Oman.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Böer |first1=Benno |last2=Chaudhary |first2=Shaukat Ali |date=1999 |title=New records for the flora of the United Arab Emirates |url=https://bioone.org/journals/willdenowia/volume-29/issue-1_2f_2/wi.29.2915/New-records-for-the-flora-of-the-United-Arab-Emirates/10.3372/wi.29.2915.pdf |journal=Willdenowia |publisher=Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum Berlin (BGBM) |volume=29 |issue=1/2 |pages=159–165 |doi=10.3372/wi.29.2915 |s2cid=85966661 |via=BioOne Complete}}</ref> She worked there until 1997, creating a herbarium (the second in the country) and supporting the [[National Herbarium of Oman]] (in the Museum of Natural History) by providing curatorial support.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=The Linnean Medal: Dr Shahina Ghazanfar, Royal Botanic Gardens Kew, Linnean Medal (Botany) 2021 |url=https://www.linnean.org/the-society/medals-awards-prizes-grants/the-linnean-medal |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=The Linnean Society |language=en |archive-date=2021-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210220003136/https://www.linnean.org/the-society/medals-awards-prizes-grants/the-linnean-medal |url-status=dead }}</ref> Ghazanfar edited the Horticultural Association of Oman and Historical Association of Oman newsletters.<ref name=":0" />

From 1997 onwards, Ghazanfar taught and researched the flora of the Arabian Peninsula, especially Oman. She had some grants from Cambridge University and [[German Academic Exchange Service|German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD)]].<ref name=":0" />

From 1999, Ghazanfar was a lecturer and researcher at the [[University of the South Pacific]] in Suva. She led a study of the plants of the islands.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" />

In 2001, Ghazanfar became an Academic Visitor to the Department of Plant Sciences in [Newnham College, Cambridge], Cambridge.<ref name=":0" />

From 2001, Ghazanfar has been based at the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]], where she is an Honorary Research Associate.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=6 April 2023 |title=London's Kew Gardens presents 'Plants of the Qur'an' exhibition |work=The Rhanuma |url=https://www.therahnuma.com/londons-kew-gardens-presents-plants-of-the-quran-exhibition/}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> She is also a Gibbs Fellow at [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College, researching on the medicinal plants of the Middle East]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Shahina Ghazanfar |url=https://newn.cam.ac.uk/person/shahina-ghazanfar/ |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=Newnham College}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Winoto |first=A |date=4 June 2023 |title=Kolaborasi Luar Biasa, di London Digelar Pameran Lukisan Tanaman yang Disebutkan Alquran |url=https://heloindonesia.com/plugin/article/view/1151/kolaborasi-luar-biasa-di-london-digelar-pameran-lukisan-tanaman-yang-disebutkan-alquran |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=Helo Indonesia |language=id}}</ref>

From 2011, she worked extensively on the Flora of Iraq project.<ref name=":1" />

In 2023, Ghazanfar's book on the plants of the Qur'an was published. The New Zealand artist Sue Wickison and Ghazanfar collaborated on an exhibition at the Shirley Sherwood Gallery at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew featuring plants named in the [[Quran|Qur'an]], which featured alongside the work of [[Anila Quayyum Agha]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-06 |title=London's Kew Gardens presents 'Plants of the Qur'an' exhibition |url=https://arab.news/rnwt2 |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=Arab News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ahmed |first=Juber |date=2023-05-25 |title=Artist Sue Wickison Goes Viral After Painting All The Plants Mentioned in The Quran |url=https://www.britishmuslim-magazine.com/2023/05/artist-sue-wickison-goes-viral-after-painting-all-the-plants-mentioned-in-the-quran/ |access-date=2023-06-13 |website=British Muslim Magazine |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

== Research and publications ==
Ghazanfar is known for her work on the vegetation and floras, [[ethnobotany]], and [[biogeography]] of plants of the Middle East.

In addition to being a researcher, lecturer and curator, Ghazanfar is a botanical artist who illustrates many of her own books and papers.<ref name=":0" />{{Botanist|Ghaz.}}

=== Selected publications ===

* ''Handbook of Arabian Medicinal Plants'' (CRC Press, 1994)
* ''Vegetation of the Arabian Peninsula'' with M. Fisher (Springer, 1998)
* ''Flora of Tropical East Africa'' (Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew Publishing)
* ''Trees of Fiji'' with Gunnar Keppel (Secretariat of the Pacific Community, 2006)
* ''Flora of Oman'' (National Botanic Garden, Belgium, 2003–2018)
* ''Flora of Iraq'' with John R. Edmondson (Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew Publishing, 2013–2019)
* ''A Herbal of Iraq'' with Chris Thorogood (Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew Publishing, 2022)
* ''Plants of the Qur'an'' illustrated by Sue Wickison (Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew Publishing, 2023)
* ''An Ancient Mesopotamian Herbal'' with Barbara Boek and Mark Nesbitt (Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew Publishing, 2023)

=== Scholarly involvement ===
In 2023 Ghazanfar was awarded the Degree of ScD (Doctor of Science) from the University of Cambridge for her work on the plants of the Middle East. She is a member of the Linnean Society and has been awarded the Linnean Medal for Botany, in 2021. She is also a member of the Association for the Taxonomic Study of the Flora of Tropical Africa, the Society for Arabian Studies, the Society of Economic Botany, and the Arabian Plant Specialist Group contributing to the Species Survival Commission of the International Union for Conservation of Nature.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite report |author= |date=2021 |title=Technical Report: UAE National Red List of Vascular Plants |url=https://www.moccae.gov.ae/assets/download/513f1b35/UAE%20National%20Red%20List%20Plants%20Report.pdf.aspx |publisher=United Arab Emirates Ministry of Climate Change and Environment |page= |docket= |access-date=13 June 2023 |quote=}}</ref>{{wikispecies|Shahina Agha Ghazanfar}}
